title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is describing the boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford compactification M̂_{g,ν} combinatorially. He uses 'MD-graphes' (Mumford–Deligne graphs), i.e. stable marked dual graphs of stable curves: a vertex set S, a genus function g: S→N, half-edges (Ã), an edge set A and marked points I. The previous page defined a 'morphisme de générisation' G' → G as the contraction of a set C' ⊂ A' of edges of G'. Contracting a loop raises the vertex genus by 1; contracting an edge between two distinct vertices merges them and adds their genera. The fibres G'_α over the vertices α of G are again marked multigraphs. G' is stable iff every G'(α) is stable, and then G is stable too. This page is a remark. (1) The definitions have been extended in passing to arbitrary multigraphs, not necessarily connected or stable, to get a cleaner statement. (2) The multigraphs obtained from G' by contraction are called the generizations, or quotient multigraphs, of G'. They form an ordered set. Via G ↔ C' this ordered set is isomorphic to the opposite of the power set P(A'). Equivalently, via G ↔ B' = A' \ C' (the surviving edges), it is isomorphic to P(A') itself. Hence G' has 2^{μ'} generizations, with μ' = card A'. (3) The 'écart' (gap) of a generization G' → G is δ = card C', the number of contracted edges. For fixed G' it takes every value from 0 to s_1(G') = card A' = the modular codimension of the stratum of G'. It is 0 iff the morphism is an isomorphism. The next page adds two things. First, every generization factors into écart-1 steps, in δ! ways (orderings of C'). Second, the generizations of G correspond to the closed strata M̂_[G'] (resp. rigidified (M̂_{G'}, Γ'^!)) containing M̂_[G]. In modern terms this is the poset of stable graphs under edge contraction, i.e. the incidence poset of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}. The codimension of a stratum equals its number of edges, and the generizations of a graph form a Boolean lattice.
errors: The bijection 'generizations ↔ subsets of A'' is correct only if generizations are counted as contraction morphisms out of a fixed G' (equivalently, subsets of edges). Up to isomorphism of the target, different edge subsets can give isomorphic quotients, for instance subsets swapped by Aut(G'). So the count 2^{μ'} is not the number of isomorphism classes of quotient graphs.

Correspondingly, the claim on the next page of a bijection between the 2^μ generizations and the closed strata M̂_[G'] containing M̂_[G] in M̂_{g,ν} fails as stated when Aut(G) permutes edges. It is correct for local branches of the boundary at a point of the stratum, and the rigidification by Γ^! only partly addresses this. On this page the statement is internally fine if read as 'subsets of edges'.
The phrase 'entre 0 et s_1(G')' presupposes s_1(G') = card A' (codimension = number of edges / nodes). That is correct for DM strata but is not restated here.

ideas.what: Generization (specialization-reversing) morphisms of stable dual graphs = edge contractions; extended to arbitrary (non-connected, non-stable) marked multigraphs
ideas.modern_name: contraction morphisms in the category of stable graphs (graph category underlying modular operads)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford / Knudsen (stratification); formalized by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Arbarello–Cornalba
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification 'à l'infini' of M̂_{g,ν} and to the Teichmüller tower, but not to this combinatorial formalism in detail

ideas.what: Poset of generizations of G' is a Boolean lattice isomorphic to the power set of the edge set; 2^{μ'} generizations
ideas.modern_name: the boundary strata containing a given stratum locally form a normal-crossings (Boolean) poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore of DM compactification / normal crossings boundary

ideas.what: 'Écart' = number of contracted edges = codimension difference; ranges from 0 to modular codimension; zero iff iso
ideas.modern_name: codimension of boundary stratum = number of edges (nodes)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard combinatorics of stable graphs and the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n}, carefully set up. The terminology ('MD-graphes', 'générisation', 'écart') is Grothendieck's own, but nothing here goes beyond what is folklore or later formalized (Getzler–Kapranov, Arbarello–Cornalba).
transcription_corrections: 'pour avoir une plus jolie insertion[?]' is more likely 'pour avoir un plus joli énoncé :' (the following words begin the statement).
'ou multigraphes génériques[?]' should read 'ou multigraphes quotients' (underlined in the image).
'Elles forment un ens. ordonné' — 'Elles' refers to the générisations; OK.
On the next page, 'MO-graphe' is an OCR misreading of 'MD-graphe'.
'{+(pour G' fixé)+}' is an interlinear insertion placed above 'est compris', which is struck out.
